messages.subject: Re: tsDyn Package query
parts:
Hi

No, it is unfortunately not possible to set specific lags to zero in the current version. Note however that this would require only minor changes to the code (i.e. setting the lags matrix, naming coeffs, and that's it!), which you can download and modify as you want!

PS: copying the tsDyn mailing list

Best

Matthieu


2013/8/23 Walsh, Graeme <graeme...@centralbank.ie>
Hi Matthieu,
 
Let me begin by saying great job on the tsDyn package and thank you for making it available to R users like myself.
 
My query is this: when using the lstar() and setar() functions from the tsDyn package, is there any way to constrain some of the lags in the model to equal zero? E.g. is it possible to estimate a model with 12 lags but set, say, the 5th and 6th lags equal to zero?
 
If you could let me know if this is possible using the tsDyn package, that’d be great.
 
Yours sincerely,
Graeme Walsh
 
 
Research Assistant
Irish Economic Analysis Division
Central Bank of Ireland
Extension: 7524

messages.author: 8c45483022d450d5
messages.subject: Re: tsDyn Package query
parts:
Dear Graeme

I realised I answered a little bit quickly! It IS actually possible to specify only a few lags, but only with the function setar(), not with lstar(), try:
setar(lynx, ML=c(1,3), MH=2)

Best

Matthieu


2013/8/24 Matthieu Stigler <matthieu...@gmail.com>

Hi

No, it is unfortunately not possible to set specific lags to zero in the current version. Note however that this would require only minor changes to the code (i.e. setting the lags matrix, naming coeffs, and that's it!), which you can download and modify as you want!

PS: copying the tsDyn mailing list

Best

Matthieu
